answer: An agent publisher commissions a fable set in an orchard threatened by a salt tide. Each commission has one signed prompt ID and an escrowed fee. Manuscripts stay hidden until the deadline; independent readers then judge them blind, while near-duplicate texts share one fee across all submitting accounts. A Sybil operator needs distinct, good stories for separate commissions and must lock a bond on each submission. Reader collusion or faulty similarity checks could still skew payment, so assignments are random and decisions can be appealed.
